question_text:
Using the data for $\alpha$-iron in  table 3.1 , compute the interplanar spacings for the (111) and (211) sets of planes.

Give your name as an answer ((111), (211)).

"Table 3.1
Atomic Radii and Crystal Structures for 16 Metals
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|l|l|}
\hline Metal & Crystal Structure ${ }^a$ & Atomic Radius ${ }^{\text {b }}$ (nm) & Metal & Crystal Structure & Atomic Radius (nm) \\
\hline Aluminum & FCC & 0.1431 & Molybdenum & BCC & 0.1363 \\
\hline Cadmium & HCP & 0.1490 & Nickel & FCC & 0.1246 \\
\hline Chromium & BCC & 0.1249 & Platinum & FCC & 0.1387 \\
\hline Cobalt & HCP & 0.1253 & Silver & FCC & 0.1445 \\
\hline Copper & FCC & 0.1278 & Tantalum & BCC & 0.1430 \\
\hline Gold & FCC & 0.1442 & Titanium ( $\alpha$ ) & HCP & 0.1445 \\
\hline Iron ( $\alpha$ ) & BCC & 0.1241 & Tungsten & BCC & 0.1371 \\
\hline Lead & FCC & 0.1750 & Zinc & HCP & 0.1332 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
${ }^a$ FCC $=$ face-centered cubic; HCP $=$ hexagonal close-packed; $\mathrm{BCC}=$ body-centered cubic. ${ }^b \mathrm{~A}$ nanometer (nm) equals $10^{-9} \mathrm{~m}$; to convert from nanometers to angstrom units ( $\AA$ ), multiply the nanometer value by 10 ."The units of each required answer are (nm, nm), respectively.
response:
## Reasoning

For α-iron from Table 3.1:
- Crystal structure: **BCC**
- Atomic radius: $R = 0.1241$ nm

**Step 1 — Lattice parameter.** For BCC, atoms touch along the body diagonal, so:
$$a = \frac{4R}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{4(0.1241)}{\sqrt{3}} = 0.2866 \text{ nm}$$

**Step 2 — Interplanar spacing.** For cubic crystals:
$$d_{hkl} = \frac{a}{\sqrt{h^2+k^2+l^2}}$$

For (111):
$$d_{111} = \frac{0.2866}{\sqrt{1+1+1}} = \frac{0.2866}{\sqrt{3}} = 0.1655 \text{ nm}$$

For (211):
$$d_{211} = \frac{0.2866}{\sqrt{4+1+1}} = \frac{0.2866}{\sqrt{6}} = 0.1433 \text{ nm}$$

$$\boxed{(0.1655, 0.1433)}$$
